items.defectStatement: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (line 12) finds the blocked record with `where(email: email)`, which is an exact, case-sensitive match. Nothing upstream normalizes case: `User.new_from_params` assigns `params[:email]` as submitted, and EmailValidator passes that value straight to should_block?. So `Bad@Spammers.org` gets past a block on `bad@spammers.org`, and the record's match_count / last_match_at are never updated.
obligations: The lookup must find the BlockedEmail record when the submitted email differs from the stored one only in letter case, at least in the domain part. For example, stored `bad@spammers.org` must match `Bad@Spammers.org` and `bad@SPAMMERS.ORG`.
Keep the current behavior once a record is found: increment match_count, set last_match_at, save, and return true only when action_type is :block. A :do_nothing record must still return false/falsy.
If no record matches, or the email is nil or blank, return falsy without raising an error. For example, calling `.downcase` on nil must not crash.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: compare case-insensitively with `lower(email) = ?` on a downcased argument, use ILIKE (but escape `%` and `_`), or normalize both the argument and the stored value with the same function. The repo's `Email.downcase` lowercases only the domain and returns invalid emails unchanged. A domain-only normalization works only if stored values are normalized the same way; a plain `where(email: Email.downcase(email))` still misses a stored entry with an uppercase local part. A full `lower()` comparison on both sides is the most robust. The finding's advice to store blocked emails in lowercase (e.g. a before_validation hook) is outside the cited line and should not be required. Note that a bare `where(email: email.downcase)` with no lower() on the column misses stored values that contain uppercase letters, which the uniqueness validation allows. Treat that as only a partial fix unless the fix also guarantees stored values are lowercase.

items.defectStatement: `totalPages` (admin-group.js.es6 lines 11-14) is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, so it is one too high whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. For example, 50 members with the default limit of 50 gives 2 pages instead of 1. Because of this, `showingLast` is false on the real last page, the `next` action moves offset to user_count and loads an empty page, and the template shows a wrong "current/total" count.
obligations: totalPages must equal ceil(user_count / limit) for every positive user_count. Exact multiples (50/50 → 1, 100/50 → 2) and non-multiples (51/50 → 2, 1/50 → 1) must both come out right.
Keep the user_count == 0 → 0 result, so that currentPage (also 0) still makes showingLast true for an empty group.
Keep the computed property dependencies on limit and user_count, so the value updates when findMembers changes them.
items.notes: The fix is limited to lines 11-14. The finding's suggested change to `next` is outside the cited range, and it is not needed: once totalPages is correct, showingLast is true on the real last page, and `next` already returns early in that case. Do not penalize a fix that leaves `next` alone. Any formula equal to ceil is fine, for example `Math.ceil(u/l)` or `Math.floor((u-1)/l)+1`. The default limit is 50 (discourse/models/group.js), and the server can override it through meta.limit.

items.defectStatement: Admin::GroupsController#remove_member removes the membership with `group.users.delete(user_id)`, but nothing clears the removed user's `primary_group_id`. The old path (usernames= plus the after_save `destroy_deletions` in group.rb:287-295) did clear it, and GroupUser has no callback that does. So a user removed this way keeps the group as their primary group (flair/title) even though they are no longer a member.
obligations: After the membership is removed, the removed user's primary_group_id must be set to NULL, but only if it currently equals this group's id. A user whose primary group is some other group must keep it.
The membership row (GroupUser) for that user and group must still be deleted.
Keep the existing behavior: automatic groups still get rejected earlier, and the success/error JSON response stays the same.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: an update_all such as `User.where(id: user_id, primary_group_id: group.id).update_all(primary_group_id: nil)` placed right after the delete, or moving the logic into Group#remove or a GroupUser after_destroy callback, as long as the cited line's replacement makes it happen. Clearing primary_group_id without checking that it equals group.id is wrong. Group#remove (group.rb:276) has the same gap, but it is out of scope here.

items.defectStatement: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members (lines 65-82), each username that resolves to a user is passed to Group#add, which calls `users.push(user)`. Because the group is already persisted, that push inserts a GroupUser row right away. If the user is already a member, or the same username appears twice in the comma-separated list, the UNIQUE index on group_users(group_id, user_id) raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and the request fails with a 500 instead of succeeding. GroupUser has no uniqueness validation, so nothing catches the duplicate earlier.
obligations: Adding a user who is already in the group must not raise and must not create a second GroupUser row; the request still returns success_json.
A username repeated in the `usernames` list (e.g. "bob,bob") must add that user only once and must not raise.

Keep the existing behavior: automatic groups are still rejected with can_not_modify_automatic before any change; unknown usernames are silently skipped; valid new users are added; the success and error responses keep their current shape.
Multiple new valid usernames in one request must all be added.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: skip users whose id is already in group.user_ids or group.users; dedupe the usernames list with uniq; use exists? / find_or_create on group_users; or make Group#add idempotent, though that last one is outside the cited lines. Rescuing RecordNotUnique per user is acceptable if it really skips the duplicate and the request still succeeds. Wrapping the loop in a transaction is a nice extra but not required. Overstated part of the finding: once duplicates are skipped there is no other realistic mid-loop failure, so a fix without a transaction should not fail grading. Trap: a fix that only checks existing membership and does not dedupe the input list (or does not refresh the membership check inside the loop) still crashes on "bob,bob". Checking `group.users.include?(user)` against the loaded association does update after each push, so that version is fine.

items.defectStatement: In the public group members route, `setupController` calls `model.findMembers()`, which uses the Group model's defaults (`limit: 50` and the current `offset`) to request `/groups/:name/members.json`. The server now applies limit/offset (default 50) to every group, and `templates/group/members.hbs` has no pagination or load-more control, so members past the first page can never be seen on the public page.
obligations: The public group members page must let users reach every member of the group. Valid approaches: fetch all members (e.g., a limit of at least user_count, or a loop over pages), or add working pagination or load-more that changes the offset and refetches.
Keep the route setup that already works: the controller model is still the group, the `group` controller's `showing` is still set to 'members', and `members` is still populated for the template.

Do not break the admin group page's paging (admin-group controller next/previous use the same Group.findMembers, limit and offset). Do not permanently change the shared model defaults in a way that changes admin behavior.
items.notes: The finding is accurate: the server's members action always applies limit (default 50) and offset. A fix limited to the cited lines can pass a large limit or reset the offset and fetch all pages. A full pagination fix would also need changes to the template and controller. Accept either approach as long as members beyond 50 become reachable. A fix that only sets the offset to 0 does not fix anything. Also watch for leftover offset state on the shared group model from earlier navigation, which could start the public view on a later page.

items.defectStatement: Lines 9-16 call `[0]['id']` and `[0]['value']` directly on the PG::Result returned by `execute`. When the query returns no rows, `result[0]` is nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError. Site settings left at their defaults are usually not stored in `site_settings`, so the `embed_category` row (or a matching category name) is often missing, which makes the first query crash on many installs. The `uncategorized_category_id` lookup has the same problem if that row is missing.
obligations: The `embed_category` lookup must not raise when the query returns zero rows. That case must count as 'no category found' and fall through to the uncategorized fallback.

The `uncategorized_category_id` fallback lookup must also not raise when it returns zero rows. It must end with some defined integer `category_id`, for example 0 or another safe default, and not crash.

Keep the existing behavior when rows exist: use the embed category's id if found, otherwise use the `uncategorized_category_id` value, converted with to_i, so later INSERTs still get an integer category_id.
items.notes: Any row-presence check is acceptable: `cmd_tuples > 0` / `ntuples > 0` (the style used at line 19), `result.first`, a `&.` / `try` chain, or `.to_a.first`. Inlining the default into SQL (e.g. COALESCE, or a subquery with a scalar fallback) is also fine. A fix that guards only the first query and leaves line 15 unguarded is incomplete. The fix doesn't need to handle SQL injection in the INSERT at line 25, which is outside the cited lines.

items.defectStatement: `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` looks up `uri.host`, which has no port. But validation accepts and keeps a `:port` suffix: before_validation removes only the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is stored as is. Such a record can never match an embed URL or referer, so `host_allowed?` (used by EmbedController and TopicRetriever) and `TopicEmbed`'s category lookup quietly fail for hosts saved with a port.
obligations: Within lines 10-18: when the URL has an explicit non-default port (e.g. `http://example.com:8080/x`), a record stored as `example.com:8080` must be found.
Hosts stored without a port must still match `http://` and `https://` URLs on default ports (existing specs: eviltrout.com matches for http and https, not-eviltrout.com does not).

Keep the existing failure behavior: return false (not raise) for URLs that can't be parsed or have no host. Return the matching record, or nil when none matches, because `topic_embed.rb` uses the record.
items.notes: The fix must replace only lines 10-18, so the realistic fix is to match on `host:port` when `uri.port != uri.default_port` (equivalent forms are fine: e.g. building the key from host and port, or querying both `host` and `host:port`). The finding's other option, rejecting ports in validation, would change line 2, which is outside the cited range. A grader could accept it only as a design note, not as a replacement for lines 10-18. Whether a URL with a port should also match a record stored without a port is a policy choice; either answer is acceptable, as long as stored `host:port` entries become reachable. Lowercasing the looked-up host is a nice extra but not required.

items.defectStatement: In the save success callback, `host.category` is set from the component's submitted `categoryId` instead of from what the server returned. When no category is chosen, `categoryId` is null. The server (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController) then stores `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` and returns it as `category_id`, but the callback runs `Category.findById(null)` and leaves `host.category` empty. The row's category badge stays blank until the page is reloaded.
obligations: After a successful save, `host.category` must be resolved from the category id the server saved and returned (e.g. `host.category_id` after `save()` applies the response payload, or the `category_id` in the response), not from the submitted `categoryId`, which can be null.
Saving with no category selected must leave `host.category` set to the Uncategorized category object, not null or undefined.
Saving with an explicitly chosen category must still show that category, and `editToggled` must still be reset to false on success.
Error handling must stay as it is: failures still go to `popupAjaxError`, and the category is not changed when the save fails.
items.notes: RestModel `update` and `_saveNew` call `setProperties` with the munged response payload, so `host.get('category_id')` holds the server value once the promise resolves. Reading it, or reading the result passed to the then-callback, are both valid fixes. A fix that falls back to `Discourse.Site.currentProp('uncategorized_category_id')` or `SiteSetting` uncategorized when `categoryId` is null is also acceptable, though less robust. A fix that only guards against null and leaves `category` unset does not solve the problem.

items.defectStatement: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the anchor check `href.start_with?('/')` (lines 64-66) also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a.png`. The leading slashes get stripped and the embed host is put in front, so the link becomes `http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/a.png` and external links in imported posts break. The img src branch at lines 70-72 has the same bug.
obligations: An href starting with '//' (protocol-relative) must not be rewritten onto the embed host. It must either stay as it is or point to the same external host (for example by adding the embed URL's scheme in front).
Root-relative hrefs with a single leading slash (e.g. '/hello') must still become prefix + path (e.g. 'http://eviltrout.com/hello'), matching the existing spec.
Absolute URLs and empty or missing hrefs must still be left alone.
items.notes: Two fixes are both valid: skip values starting with '//', or resolve them against the embed URL's scheme (e.g. with URI.join). The fix covers only lines 64-66 (the anchor block). The img src block at lines 70-72 has the same bug, but changes there are outside the cited range and should not be required. A fix that still strips every leading slash for '//' input fails the first obligation.

items.defectStatement: In TopicEmbed.import, line 13 puts the raw `url` into a single-quoted href attribute and into the link text with no HTML escaping. The post is then cooked as raw_html. A URL with a quote or angle brackets, such as `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` or one containing `<script>`, can break out of the attribute or text and store XSS in the post. The URL comes from the embed request (via TopicRetriever/import_remote) or from RSS feed item links (PollFeed), and those inputs only get a host or scheme check.
obligations: The URL must be HTML-escaped (at least `'`, `"`, `<`, `>`, `&`) in both places: the href attribute value and the link text. Another option is to build the anchor with a DOM builder that escapes attributes and text itself.
A normal http(s) URL must still produce a working link whose href points to the same URL, wrapped in the 'embed.imported_from' message inside <small> after <hr>.
Do not change the `url` value used for the TopicEmbed lookup, the embed_url storage or absolutize_urls. Escape only the copy that goes into the HTML.
items.notes: Valid fixes include ERB::Util.html_escape / CGI.escapeHTML on url in both spots, or building the <a> with Nokogiri. Escaping only the href and leaving the link text raw is incomplete, because `<script>` in the path could still be injected through the text. Switching to double quotes without escaping does not fix anything. URL-encoding (URI.escape) is also acceptable if it reliably neutralizes quotes and angle brackets, but HTML escaping is the expected approach. Rejecting such URLs in an earlier validation step is out of scope for these lines.

items.defectStatement: TopicEmbed.import_remote passes the embed_url to Kernel#open (open-uri) without checking it. The URL comes from the public EmbedController#best → Jobs::RetrieveTopic → TopicRetriever path. The only upstream guard, TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, compares just the hostname to SiteSetting.embeddable_host. The scheme, port and redirect targets are never checked, and there is no timeout, so the server can be made to request arbitrary ports on that host or follow redirects to internal addresses (SSRF).
obligations: The fetch at line 48 must only happen for http/https URLs. Non-HTTP schemes, and strings that Kernel#open would treat as a file path or a `|command` pipe, must not be opened.
The fetch must not follow redirects to unvalidated targets. Either disable redirects, or re-validate each redirect location (scheme, host, and no private/loopback/link-local address).
Destination checks must run before any request is made. Acceptable checks include: no private/loopback/link-local IPs, the host matching embeddable_host, and/or only default or allowed ports.

Valid embeddable-host http(s) URLs must still be fetched, with the body passed to Readability::Document using the same tags/attributes and then on to TopicEmbed.import with opts[:title] || doc.title. A timeout is desirable.
items.notes: Valid fixes can use open-uri with `redirect: false` plus scheme/host/IP validation, Net::HTTP / Excon / FinalDestination-style resolution with checks, or URI.parse(url).open in place of Kernel#open together with validation. A fix only has to change the cited line, so validation can sit inline or in a helper that line calls. A port-only check at line 48 is not enough if redirects are still followed. The finding's example (eviltrout.com:6379) depends on embeddable_host being set to that host, so the port-based SSRF is limited to the configured host. The redirect-to-internal case is the more serious one. Simply swapping Kernel#open for URI.open still follows redirects, so that alone is not enough.

items.defectStatement: On lines 40-42 of lib/topic_retriever.rb, `perform_retrieve` handles a lookup for one embed URL that isn't known yet by running the whole feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`). That poll downloads and parses the full RSS feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` on every item, with no early exit once `@embed_url` has been handled. So each retrieval costs O(N) DB lookups, plus topic creations or revisions for any new or changed items, when only one item matters.
obligations: The feed step should stop doing per-item import work for unrelated items once the target `@embed_url` is found. For example: stop iterating after the match, only import items whose URL matches `@embed_url`, or pass the target URL into the job so it can filter.
Keep the fallback: if the feed doesn't produce a TopicEmbed for `@embed_url`, `fetch_http` must still run. If it does, return without fetching over HTTP.

Only check the feed when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. The feed's URL matching (use `i.link`, or `i.id` when the link is blank or not http/https) and the import of the matching item must work exactly as before.
The scheduled hourly `PollFeed` run (`execute({})` with no target) must still import every feed item.
items.notes: The finding is partly overstated. `TopicEmbed.import` only does a lookup for items that already exist, and writes only when an item is new or its content SHA changed. So the "heavy writes" happen mainly for new or changed items, though the full fetch, parse and per-item lookup cost is real. The finding also implies this runs on the embed view's request path. It doesn't: TopicRetriever runs inside the background `retrieve_topic` job, which EmbedController enqueues, and non-staff calls are throttled to once per 60s per URL. A full fix may need changes in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, such as an optional embed_url arg or a break condition. Accept that, as long as the cited call site passes the target URL or otherwise limits the work. An alternative is to have TopicRetriever parse the feed itself and import only the matching item; that is also valid. Do not accept a fix that just drops feed polling for the target URL, because that changes behavior.

items.defectStatement: Line 35 calls `i.content.scrub` without checking for nil. SimpleRSS only fills `content` from an Atom `<content>` element, so a normal RSS 2.0 item that has only `<description>` (or only `<content:encoded>`, which SimpleRSS exposes as `content_encoded`) has `i.content == nil`, and the call raises NoMethodError. That one item stops the whole `rss.items.each` loop. The job has `retry: false`, so nothing else from the feed gets imported, and the exception also reaches `TopicRetriever`, which runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41).
obligations: An item whose `content` is nil must not raise. The fix must fall back to another body field: at least `i.description`, optionally `content_encoded`.

If an item has no usable body at all (every candidate is nil or blank), skip that item (e.g. `next`) and keep processing the rest of the feed. Do not call `.scrub` or `CGI.unescapeHTML` on nil, and do not pass nil to `TopicEmbed.import`, which appends to its `contents` argument with `<<`.

Items that do have `content` (Atom) must keep the current behavior: scrub, then `CGI.unescapeHTML`, then pass the result to `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. `content` should be preferred when it is present.
items.notes: The finding says `content:encoded` sets `content`. In SimpleRSS that tag actually maps to `content_encoded`, but the conclusion still holds: RSS 2.0 items get a nil `content`. Accept either fallback order (content || content_encoded || description, or content || description). Accept either a `next if blank?` skip or an equivalent guard. Using `next` inside the `each` block is fine. A fix that just swaps in `.to_s` without skipping or falling back is incomplete: it would import empty posts and ignore the description. Wrapping each item in a rescue is acceptable only if items with only a description still get imported through the fallback.

items.defectStatement: In EmbedController#best (lines 14-16), any request whose embed_url has no TopicEmbed yet enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no limit at the controller level. The only throttle is in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?, which uses a 60s Redis key per exact URL, so every new path or query string gets through. Each job that gets through also runs Jobs::PollFeed synchronously (it downloads and imports the whole RSS feed) and then fetches the remote URL over HTTP. As a result, unauthenticated traffic can trigger unbounded job, RSS and HTTP fanout. The Referer check in ensure_embeddable is a header the client controls, and it does not stop this.
obligations: Before calling Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...), the fixed code must apply a limit that does not depend on the exact embed_url, keyed per client IP and/or globally, so that many distinct URLs cannot each enqueue a job without bound.
When the limit is exceeded, the code must not enqueue a job. Rendering 'loading', returning 429, or a similar response is acceptable, and the request must not raise an unhandled 500.

Normal behavior must be kept: if topic_id exists, the TopicView is still built. If it does not and the request is under the limit, the job is still enqueued with user_id and embed_url, and 'loading' is rendered. discourse_expires_in still runs.
Anonymous users must be handled. Do not call something that dereferences current_user.id when current_user is nil.
items.notes: The existing RateLimiter (lib/rate_limiter.rb) builds its key from user.id, so it cannot be used directly for anonymous users. A valid fix needs an IP- or global-keyed Redis counter, or a RateLimiter wrapper with a key that does not use the user. Exempting staff is optional, and it is fine either way. The finding's second suggestion, running PollFeed at most once per interval, lives in lib/topic_retriever.rb, outside the cited lines. A cited-lines fix should not be marked down for leaving it out. A fix that limits only per exact URL, or only checks the Referer, does not address the defect. Also checking in the controller that the embed_url host is the embeddable host is a fine addition, but it is not enough alone, because one host has unlimited paths.

items.defectStatement: In mobile/user.scss line 497, the `.group-member-info .name` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to a `dark-light-choose` whose light branch uses 50%. That makes member names lighter in the light theme, when the point of the change was only to add dark-theme support. It also makes `.name` look the same as `.title`, which was meant to be styled lighter.
obligations: The light-theme (first/primary) value must be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, the same as the original light-theme color.
Keep dark-theme support: the value should stay a `dark-light-choose(...)` with a `$secondary`-based dark branch. The codebase convention for 30% primary is `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.
Leave the other properties of the rule unchanged: display, margin-top and vertical-align.
items.notes: The convention `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` appears in common/base/user.scss, header.scss and topic-post.scss. A grader can accept a slightly different dark value, but the light value must be 30%. Do not penalize a fix for leaving the `.title` rule (line 503) at 50%, because that matches its original value.

items.defectStatement: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss line 522 (`.group-member-info .name`), the PR replaced the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with a `dark-light-choose(...)` whose light-theme argument is 50%. On the light theme the member name now renders as the lighter medium gray used for `.title`, not the darker 30% shade it had before, so this is an unintended visual regression.
obligations: The light-theme (first) argument of dark-light-choose on line 522 must be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, which restores the original light-theme color.

The rule must still use dark-light-choose so dark themes get a secondary-based color. The dark-theme argument should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`, the inverse pairing used elsewhere in the codebase.
Only the `.name` color changes. The `.title` rule and the other lines in this rule stay as they are.
items.notes: The finding is correct. The diff shows the original value was 30%. The pairing `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` is already used in common/base/user.scss, header.scss, topic-post.scss and mobile/modal.scss. A dark-theme argument close to 70% secondary can be accepted. Leaving it at 50% is a weaker fix, but the main requirement is restoring the light-theme value to 30%.

items.defectStatement: In mobile/modal.scss line 102, `.custom-message-length` uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The percentages are swapped. The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, and the matching desktop/modal.scss rule (line 94) uses 70% for the light theme and 30% for the dark theme. As written, light-theme users get darker hint text than before, and the dark-theme color doesn't match desktop.
obligations: The light-theme (first) argument must be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, the same as the original value, so light-theme output does not change.
The dark-theme (second) argument must be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`, matching desktop/modal.scss.
Keep the `dark-light-choose(light, dark)` argument order, since the function returns the first argument when $primary is darker than $secondary. Do not revert to a single color with no theme switch.
items.notes: `dark-light-choose` is defined in common/foundation/variables.scss: the first argument is the light-theme result and the second is the dark-theme result. The finding is accurate. The expected fix is exactly the desktop line. Other equivalent ways of computing the same two colors are acceptable.

items.defectStatement: `include_website_name` (lines 153-155) has no trailing `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializers never calls it as a filter and `website_name` is always serialized. `website` is hidden by `untrusted_attributes` through `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (lines 25-33, 109), but `website_name` is not, so the website's host and path still reach viewers who should not see them (e.g. anonymous visitors looking at TL0 users).
obligations: website_name must not be serialized when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true, the same rule that hides website.
website_name must still be included when the user has a website and the viewer is not restricted.
website_name must not be included (or must be nil) when the website is blank.
The include filter must be a predicate named `include_website_name?`, or come from the untrusted_attributes macro, so ActiveModel::Serializers actually calls it.
items.notes: The fix only replaces lines 153-155, so the expected fix is something like `def include_website_name?; website.present? && !scope.restrict_user_fields?(object); end`. Equivalent forms are fine, such as returning false early when restricted and otherwise checking `website.present?` or `website_name.present?`. Adding :website_name to untrusted_attributes at line 105 also fixes it, but that line is outside the cited range. If the fix keeps that approach, the leftover method must not conflict with the macro-defined `include_website_name?`. Only renaming the method to add `?` while keeping just `website.present?` does NOT fix the leak.

items.defectStatement: In `website_name` (lines 144-146), two hosts count as siblings whenever they have the same number of labels (more than 2) and match after the first label is dropped. When the forum runs on a public-suffix domain, an unrelated site passes this check: `forum.co.uk` and `evil.co.uk` both reduce to `co.uk`. The serializer then returns host plus full path for an external site, when it should return the bare host.
obligations: Two hosts whose shared remainder is only a public suffix (e.g. website `evil.co.uk` with forum `forum.co.uk`, or `a.com.au` with `b.com.au`) must not count as the same domain. website_name must return only the website host, without the path.

Real sibling subdomains of one registrable domain must still get host + path, e.g. website `www.example.com/user` with forum `forum.example.com` gives `www.example.com/user`, and `www.example.co.uk` with `forum.example.co.uk` still matches.

Do not change the other branches: an exact host match returns host + path, and an unrelated domain (e.g. discourse.org vs example.com) returns just the host. A nil or unparseable host still returns nil.
items.notes: The finding is correct. The public_suffix gem is not currently in the repo, so a fix can add it, use another registrable-domain helper, or use a reasonable heuristic. The finding's alternative, "require at least three labels after removing the subdomain", is a trap if applied literally: `www.example.com` and `forum.example.com` reduce to `example.com`, which has only two labels, so the intended feature would break. Accept a heuristic only if it rejects co.uk-style suffixes and still matches example.com siblings. The else branch on line 149 has a similar flaw: a website host of `co.uk` with forum `forum.example.co.uk` passes `ends_with?`. It also mutates a string literal with `<<`. Line 149 is outside the cited lines, so a fix need not address it. Existing specs in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb lines 77-90 must keep passing.

items.defectStatement: In `website_name`'s fallback branch (line 149), the only check is `discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host)`, which matches only when the website host is a parent of the instance host. When the website is a subdomain of the instance (e.g. website `forum.example.com/user`, instance `example.com`), the check is false, so the method returns just `forum.example.com` and drops the path, even though the site is on the same domain.
obligations: When website_host is a subdomain of discourse_host on a dot boundary (e.g. website forum.example.com, instance example.com), return website_host + the URI path.

Keep the existing parent case: website example.com with instance forums.example.com must still return 'example.com/user'. Unrelated domains (website example.com, instance discourse.org) must still return the bare host.
Both directions must be checked on a label/dot boundary. A plain suffix check is not enough: e.g. notexample.com vs example.com, or evilforum.example.com, must not count as the same domain.
Return type and shape stay the same: a string of host plus optional path. Lines outside the cited else branch are untouched.
items.notes: `"." << website_host` creates a new string and does not mutate website_host, so it is not a bug in itself. Rewriting it as `"." + website_host` is fine. Any valid way to check both directions is acceptable: two ends_with? calls joined with `||`, a helper, or comparing split labels. The existing spec only covers the same-host, parent and unrelated cases, so this is partly a design gap rather than a regression, but the finding is valid given the method's same-domain intent. A fix that drops the dot boundary (e.g. `website_host.ends_with?(discourse_host)`) should be marked down.

items.defectStatement: In validateUploadedFile (utilities.js lines 180-186), the client-side size limit is hardcoded to 10*1024 KB and no longer reads Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. Because of this, the configured max_image_size_kb and max_attachment_size_kb are ignored. Files over the configured limit pass the check whenever that limit is under 10 MB, and files are rejected whenever the configured limit is over 10 MB. The error message also reports the wrong maximum.
obligations: The max size must come from the site setting for the given type: max_image_size_kb when type is 'image' and max_attachment_size_kb when type is 'attachment'. It must not be a hardcoded constant.
The file_too_large alert must report the same per-type limit that was used in the comparison, and the function must still return false when the file is too large.
Keep the current behavior otherwise: compare file.size/1024 against the limit in KB, and return true for files at or under the limit.
items.notes: test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6 sets max_image_size_kb=5, or 15 and max_attachment_size_kb=1, and expects per-type rejection. The hardcoded value breaks those tests. Any equivalent lookup counts as a valid fix, for example a conditional on type that picks the matching setting. The 413 branch in displayErrorForUpload (around line 246) has a similar hardcoded value, but it is outside the cited lines, so a fix does not need to change it.

items.defectStatement: Lines 63-70 rewrite the image at `tempfile.path` while the Tempfile is still open, then check `tempfile.size` (fstat on the open descriptor). `OptimizedImage.downsize` → `convert_with` ends with `ImageOptim#optimize_image!(to)`, and ImageOptim swaps in its result by renaming a new file over the path. After that rename the descriptor still points at the old, unlinked inode, which only holds ImageMagick's intermediate output. So the loop guard and the `tempfile.size` passed to `Upload.create_for` as `filesize` (line 72) can be stale, and so can the bytes `create_for` reads from the IO (FastImage). Meanwhile the stored file (`File.open(file.path)`) and the SHA1 come from the new file at the path, so the stored `filesize` and the dimensions can disagree with the bytes actually stored.
obligations: After each downsize, the size check that decides whether to keep looping must use the file currently at `tempfile.path` (e.g. `File.size(tempfile.path)`, or reopen/rewind the tempfile onto the new file), not a size read from a descriptor that may be stale.

Whatever size and file handle reach `Upload.create_for` after downsizing must match the downsized file at the path. That means not passing the pre-rename descriptor's size and not leaving a stale IO that FastImage would read.

Keep the existing behaviour: the guard conditions (tempfile present, non-empty, `max_image_size_kb > 0`, image filename), the limit of 5 attempts, the "80%" resize with `allow_animation`, non-image and small-file uploads left untouched, and `tempfile.close!` cleanup in the `ensure` block.
items.notes: The finding blames ImageMagick for writing a new inode. `convert` usually rewrites the file in place; the inode actually changes in the ImageOptim step inside `OptimizedImage.convert_with`. So the stale size is ImageMagick's intermediate output, not always the original file. Either way the defect is real. Valid fixes include: checking `File.size(tempfile.path)` in the loop and passing that value to `create_for`; downsizing to a separate path and then reopening the tempfile or replacing the file at its path; or reopening the Tempfile (`tempfile.open`) after each pass. A fix that only changes the loop guard but still passes the stale `tempfile.size` to `create_for` is incomplete. Fixes outside the cited lines (e.g. inside `Upload.create_for`) are out of scope. `create_for` already uses the same in-place pattern for cropped image types, so that pattern is not proof of correctness.

items.defectStatement: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is routed as GET (`config/routes.rb:440-441`), and it changes data: it lowers the user's `TopicUser.notification_level` (watching/tracking → regular, regular → muted) and calls `save!` with no CSRF token, signed token or confirmation step. Any third-party page can embed `` and silently change, and eventually mute, notifications on any topic for a logged-in victim.
obligations: A cross-site GET to /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe (or /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe) with only the victim's session cookie must not change the TopicUser notification_level.

The notification change must be gated by one of: a CSRF-protected non-GET request (POST/PUT), an explicit user confirmation that then submits such a request, or a signed per-user/per-topic token checked before saving.

The unsubscribe link in notification emails (`Topic#unsubscribe_url`, used in `user_notifications.rb`) must still let a user reach the action and unsubscribe, e.g. the GET shows the topic with a confirmation, or the token is included in the emailed URL.
Keep the existing slug-redirect behavior and the regular/muted lowering logic for legitimate requests.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: move the mutation to a POST/PUT that has CSRF protection and make the GET render only the page or a confirmation, or require a signed token (similar to `email#unsubscribe/:key`). If the fix replaces only the cited lines, the GET routes in routes.rb may still need changing. A grader should accept a controller-side fix that refuses to mutate on GET, for example a GET that renders without saving and a separate verified path that saves. Separate issue that should not be held against the fix: `tu` can be nil when no TopicUser row exists, which raises NoMethodError. Fixing it is nice but not required.

items.defectStatement: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` (line 105) returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic. That happens when someone gets an email about a topic they never opened. Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, and lines 108-113 also dereference `tu`, so the unsubscribe link raises NoMethodError (500).
obligations: When no TopicUser row exists for (current_user, topic), the action must not raise. After the replacement lines, `tu` must be a usable record, or the missing case must be handled some other way, because the untouched lines 108-113 assign `tu.notification_level` and call `tu.save!`.
A missing record must count as the default level (regular). Unsubscribing then sets the level to muted, and that result must be saved (a new row created or found).
Existing behavior must stay the same when a record exists: a level above regular (tracking/watching) drops to regular, and a level of regular or below becomes muted.
The lookup must still be scoped to current_user.id and the requested topic_id.
items.notes: The finding suggests using TopicUser.get, but that will not fix it: TopicUser.get (app/models/topic_user.rb:68) is just a wrapper around find_by and also returns nil. Fixes that work include `TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by(...)` / `find_or_create_by`, or building a new TopicUser with notification_level regular when none exists. If a new record is initialized, its notification_level must not be nil when compared at line 107; either rely on a DB default or set regular explicitly, e.g. `(tu.notification_level || regular) > regular`. Notification levels: muted=0, regular=1, tracking=2, watching=3. A fix that just returns early or skips when tu is nil, leaving the user subscribed, does not meet the unsubscribe intent.

items.defectStatement: The `topicUnsubscribe` route's `model` hook (lines 4-8) calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`. That function returns the preloaded topic if the page was loaded from the server, and otherwise requests `/t/:id.json`, the ordinary topic-show endpoint. The notification level is only lowered by `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (GET `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, which drops it to regular, or to muted if it was already regular or lower). So the change only happens on a full page load of the unsubscribe URL. On an in-app transition, the page shows the "you will stop receiving notifications" text but the user's TopicUser notification level never changes.
obligations: On a client-side transition, the route must actually lower the notification level before the confirmation is shown. Either send a request to the server unsubscribe action (e.g. GET `/t/:id/unsubscribe.json`; the action accepts JSON and returns the topic view) or change the level some other way, such as through the topic's notification-level update.

The model hook must still resolve to a topic record filled in from the returned topic JSON (`updateFromJson`), so the template (`fancyTitle`, the topic-notifications-button) and `afterModel` (`details.notificationReasonText`) keep working.

Full page loads must not unsubscribe twice. The server has already changed the level and preloaded `topic_<id>`, and a second call would push a regular level down to muted. A fix must reuse the preloaded data (e.g. through PreloadStore) or otherwise avoid a second preference change.
The confirmation must not be shown if the unsubscribe request fails. Let the rejected promise propagate, or show an error.
items.notes: How the bug arises: `loadTopicView` uses `PreloadStore.getAndRemove("topic_"+id, ...)`, so on a hard load it returns the data the server preloaded after `#unsubscribe` already ran. A client-side transition skips the server action and falls back to `/t/:id.json`. Valid fixes include calling `Discourse.ajax('/t/' + id + '/unsubscribe.json')` (or a `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe.json` URL) wrapped in PreloadStore.getAndRemove, or adding an explicit confirm/submit step on the page. A fix that merely adds a separate unsubscribe ajax call next to the unchanged `loadTopicView` call is wrong if it also fires on hard loads, because the server toggles regular→muted on the second call. Watch slug handling: the server redirects when the slug doesn't match, but for JSON requests a blank slug is allowed.

items.defectStatement: The fallback chain in FallbackLocaleList#[] (line 17) reads SiteSetting.default_locale on every call. But I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb caches results in a process-wide LRU keyed only by `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. A string that fell back to the site locale stays cached under the user's locale. After an admin changes default_locale, or in a multisite process serving sites with different default locales, the old or wrong site-locale text keeps being served. Nothing clears the cache when the setting changes: only I18n.reload! resets @cache.
obligations: After SiteSetting.default_locale changes, I18n.t for a key missing in the user's locale must return the new default locale's text (or :en), not a value cached from the old default locale. This can be done by including the default locale (or the full fallback chain) in the cache key, or by invalidating/resetting the cache on change.
The fallback order must stay as it is: user locale first, then the site default locale, then :en, with duplicates removed and nils dropped.
Translation caching must keep working for the common no-args path, and calls with args must keep bypassing the cache.
items.notes: The finding is correct. The real fix lives in translate_accelerator.rb (the cache key at line 72) or in a hook that runs on a setting change (e.g. I18n.reload! or clearing @cache when default_locale changes). It cannot be fixed by editing line 17 alone. A replacement for line 17 that only reorders or rewrites the array does not fix the bug. Both valid approaches are fine: adding the default locale to the key, or invalidating the cache on change. Bonus, not required: multisite processes share the cache, so a key that includes the default locale handles both cases, while a single-process cache clear does not fully handle multisite or other worker processes.

items.defectStatement: Locale files are loaded lazily, and `I18n.translate` (translate_accelerator.rb:68) only loads `config.locale`. The fallback chain (user locale → `SiteSetting.default_locale` → :en) is only loaded by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`, and that is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Code outside a web request (Jobs::Base setting `I18n.locale=`, PostAlerter's `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`, PostDestroyer, mailers) can go through I18n::Backend::Fallbacks to locales that were never loaded in that process, so lookups that should fall back still come back as "translation missing".
obligations: Every fallback locale for the current locale (current locale, site default locale, :en) must be loaded before a translation is looked up. This must hold in all code paths, including jobs, PostAlerter, mailers and `with_locale` blocks, not just controller requests.
Keep loading lazy and once per locale per process (the `@loaded_locales` / LOAD_MUTEX behavior). Do not reload on every call.
Web requests must keep working: `set_locale` still sets `I18n.locale` from the user's effective locale or the site default, and still ends up with the fallback chain loaded.
items.notes: The finding is valid. A change limited to line 159 of application_controller.rb cannot fix the non-request paths. A correct fix has to make loading safe in a shared place: for example, have `I18n.translate`/`load_locale` load every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]` instead of only `config.locale` (translate_accelerator.rb:68). Another option is to hook `ensure_loaded!` into the `locale=` / `with_locale` paths. Adding `ensure_loaded!` calls at each known call site (jobs/base.rb:151, post_alerter.rb:138, post_destroyer.rb:102) is weaker but acceptable if all of them are covered. If a fix only rewrites line 159, the defect is not fixed. `@loaded_locales` is process-global, so the problem mostly shows up in Sidekiq or other non-web processes. Watch the caching too: the LRU cache key in translate includes the locale, so a fix should not cache a 'missing' result made before the fallbacks were loaded.

items.defectStatement: In GroupPermissionsV2, the no-arg canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). hasPermission returns true when any listed scope is granted, so an admin who holds only the all-groups VIEW permission passes canManage(), which makes it the same as canView(). Because GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls groups().requireManage(), which uses canManage(), a view-only group admin can create top-level groups (privilege escalation).
obligations: The fine-grained fallback in canManage() must succeed only when the all-groups MANAGE scope is granted. VIEW alone must no longer be enough.
Keep the early return true for admins with the MANAGE_USERS role.
Keep the behavior where an all-groups MANAGE permission (hasPermission with groupId null) makes canManage() return true.
Leave canView() unchanged: it still accepts VIEW or MANAGE.
items.notes: The expected fix is hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), which matches canManage(GroupModel) and ClientPermissionsV2.canManage. The finding says "create/update/delete groups", which is overstated. In production code, only addTopLevelGroup calls the no-arg requireManage() (GroupsResource.java:181). Update and delete use the per-group canManage(group), which is already correct. Do not accept a fix that removes the MANAGE_USERS role check, or that adds VIEW_MEMBERS or other unrelated scopes.

items.defectStatement: At lines 121-125, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses groupResource.getId(), which is the internal UUID of the authorization resource. But AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() names each group resource with the group id (resolveGroup returns group.getId()), and hasPermission() looks resources up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Because of this, the per-group lookup never finds the resource and falls back to the all-groups resource. The returned set also holds resource UUIDs rather than group ids, so callers that filter users by group (UsersResource search/count, BruteForceUsersResource) match no users, or the wrong ones.
obligations: Both the value passed to hasPermission and the value added to the returned set must be the group id, i.e. the resource name (groupResource.getName()), not the resource's internal id.
Keep the existing permission check: a group is included only when the per-group resource (or the all-groups fallback) grants VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS.
Keep iterating over GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE resources with resourceStore.findByType, and leave the early-return behavior (emptySet) in the lines before the cited block unchanged.
items.notes: The finding is correct. getOrCreateResource creates resources with name = group id, and hasPermission uses findByName. Both getId() calls must change. A fix that changes only the add() call, or only the hasPermission call, is incomplete. Calling getName() once and reusing the result in both places is fine. Optional extras that are acceptable but not required: skipping the type-level "Groups" resource if findByType returns it, or checking that the group exists.

items.defectStatement: The diff is right that getSubGroups (GroupResource.java:176-180) now calls auth.groups().canView(g) for every subgroup instead of checking the global canView() once. The cost is mostly overstated, though. V1 GroupPermissions.canView(group) first checks canView()/canManage(), which are cheap admin-role checks, and V2 GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) returns early for MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS. The only real extra work is in V2 for admins whose access comes only from an "all-groups" permission: each subgroup costs one resource lookup and one evaluatePermission call. Note that because pagination is applied after the filter, the evaluations run over all filtered subgroups, not just one page.
obligations: Do not let a global V2 canView() result (which can be true just because of an all-groups permission) skip per-group evaluation, because a group-specific permission (e.g. a NEGATIVE/deny policy on that group's resource) must still be able to hide that subgroup from the listing.

Keep requireView(group) on the parent group, the per-subgroup visibility filter, the search/exact handling, the order of filtering before pagination (first/max), and the representation mapping (briefRepresentation, populateSubGroupCount).

Any fast path that is added must only skip per-group checks when the caller can see every group without exception (e.g. holds the MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS admin roles). It must return exactly the same subgroups as checking canView(g) on each one.
items.notes: Removing the short-circuit looks deliberate. In V2, canView() evaluates the all-groups type resource, while canView(g) evaluates that group's own resource when one exists, so a specific deny can override an all-groups grant. Simply restoring `canViewGlobal || canView(g)` would bring back an authorization bypass in V2, so a grader should reject that fix. V1 already short-circuits inside canView(group), so V1 sees no meaningful regression. Acceptable responses: keep the current code and argue that the finding is overstated; add a short-circuit based only on admin roles; or precompute the group ids, which is also valid if it gives the same results. Pagination happens after the filter, so the extra cost covers all subgroups that match the search, not only one page.

items.defectStatement: In V2, group resources are named with the bare group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource → resolveGroup returns group.getId()). But the set returned by getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() goes to UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource → JpaUserProvider search/count, and its groupsWithPermissionsSubquery also requires that a ResourceEntity named "group.resource." + groupId exists. So for an admin whose access comes only from V2 group permissions (view-members/manage-members), user search and count return no members even when the group IDs are correct. On top of that, the method fills the set with groupResource.getId() (the internal authz resource id), not the group ID (the resource name), and passes that same resource id to hasPermission, which looks the resource up by name.
obligations: For an admin whose only access comes from V2 per-group view-members/manage-members permissions, user search and count (UsersResource getUsers/getUsersCount, and the BruteForceUsersResource path) must return and count the members of the permitted groups. This means the JPA filter must stop requiring a legacy "group.resource.<id>" resource for V2 (for example: skip the resource-name EXISTS check when V2 is active, accept bare-ID resource names, or rely only on the pre-authorized group-ID set).

The set returned by GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() must contain real group IDs (the V2 resource name / group id), not internal authorization resource ids, and the per-resource permission check must find the specific group resource.

V1 behavior must be kept: GroupPermissions (V1) results and JPA filtering with legacy "group.resource.<id>" resources must keep working, and the empty-set short-circuits (users().canView(), admin not in the same realm, no resource server) must stay as they are.
items.notes: The finding is correct: JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery (around line 1081) hardcodes cb.concat("group.resource.", groupId). The cited line (`return granted;`) cannot fix this by itself. A real fix has to touch JpaUserProvider's filtering contract, or change what the group-ID set means. Several approaches are valid: drop or relax the resource-name check, add a V2-aware branch, or match both the prefixed and bare names. A fix that only changes line 127 (for example, mapping to names) without making the JPA filter accept V2 resources does not solve the reported problem. Related bug in the same method: granted.add(groupResource.getId()) and hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) use the resource id where the resource name is the group ID. Fixing that is welcome but does not resolve the JPA mismatch on its own. Also, V2 resources created by getOrCreateResource may not have their type set to "Groups", so findByType could miss them. A grader may accept a fix that addresses this too, but it is not required by the finding.

items.defectStatement: In ClientPermissionsV2, canView() (lines 85-88) returns true only for the MANAGE_CLIENTS/VIEW_CLIENTS admin roles or a VIEW-scope grant on the all-clients resource. A FGAP v2 grant of MANAGE on all-clients does not count. So an admin who has canManage()==true still gets canView()==false, and canList()/canListClientScopes() and requireView()/requireList() (which rely on canView()) turn them away. That is inconsistent with V1 (manage implies view), with canView(ClientScopeModel) in this class (VIEW || MANAGE), and with canView(ClientModel), which already passes through canConfigure→canManage(client).
obligations: canView() must return true when the caller has the MANAGE scope granted on the all-clients resource type, even without VIEW (for example by adding a check for hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), or by delegating to canManage()).
Existing grants must keep working: canView() still returns true for the MANAGE_CLIENTS or VIEW_CLIENTS admin roles (canViewClientDefault()) and for an all-clients VIEW grant.

Do not widen access beyond global VIEW/MANAGE. A MANAGE or VIEW grant on a single client must not make the global canView() true. Callers that combine canView() with the rest of the canView(ClientModel) logic must not end up recursing forever.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: `|| hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, or `|| canManage()` (canManage() = super.canManage() [MANAGE_CLIENTS role] || hasPermission(MANAGE)). Both are fine because canManage() does not call canView(). The finding is accurate. canList() in the parent ClientPermissions is canView() || QUERY_* roles, so fixing canView() also fixes listing.

items.defectStatement: `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` (lines 136-144) only looks up resources with type "Clients". `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates per-client resources with no type (name = client internal id), so none of them are ever found. The only resource that can match is the all-clients resource, whose name is "Clients". That means a granted per-client permission is never returned. If the all-clients permission is granted, the string "Clients" is returned, and the caller (`AvailableRoleMappingResource:230`) then calls `realm.getClientById("Clients").getRolesStream()` and fails with an NPE.
obligations: For every client whose per-client V2 resource (an untyped resource named with the client's internal id) gives the caller the requested scope, the returned set must include that client's internal id (`ClientModel.getId()`), because the caller resolves each value with `realm.getClientById`.
The returned set must never contain the resource-type name "Clients" or any other value that is not a client id.

Keep the early returns: an empty set when the admin is not in the same realm (`!isAdminSameRealm`) or when `realmResourceServer()` is null. A granted scope must still be checked by evaluating the permission for the requested scope, as `hasGrantedPermission` does.
items.notes: The finding's HOW suggests mapping to `client.getClientId()`. That is wrong: V1 strips the resource-name prefix, which gives the internal `client.getId()`, and the caller uses `getClientById`. A fix that returns the human-readable clientId is incorrect. Several fixes are valid: (a) set the type to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE on per-client resources in `getOrCreateResource` (this is outside the cited lines, and the all-clients resource still has to be filtered out), (b) loop over the realm's clients and use the existing `hasPermission(client, scope)`, which also covers the all-clients fallback, or (c) go through the resource server's resources, skip the type resource, and check that each name resolves to a client. Expanding an all-clients grant to every realm client is acceptable but not required. Simply filtering out the "Clients" name while keeping the `findByType` lookup is not a valid fix, because it still returns nothing for per-client grants.

items.defectStatement: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists, the code falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...). That call can return null: when the server doesn't support the authorization schema, when the type is unknown, or when the "Clients" type resource is missing. The null is then passed straight to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). The cached store calls resource.getId() and throws a NullPointerException, so the permission check crashes instead of returning false.
obligations: When the fallback getResourceTypeResource(...) returns null, hasPermission(ClientModel, String) must return false and must not call findByResource or evaluate with a null resource.
When the fallback resource is non-null and has no associated policies, the method must still return false, as it does now.
When the fallback resource is non-null and has policies, evaluation must still go ahead using that all-clients resource. The path where a per-client resource is found must be unchanged.
items.notes: I confirmed the null returns in AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource (lines 116-134). The NPE happens at resource.getId() in StoreFactoryCacheSession.findByResource (line 938). Any equivalent null guard is valid, for example `resource == null || findByResource(...).isEmpty()`. UserPermissionsV2 (lines 121-123) has the same defect, but it is outside the cited lines, so a fix doesn't need to touch it.

items.defectStatement: In ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel), lines 78-79 return true as soon as the global canView() is true. canView() includes hasPermission(VIEW) on the "all clients" type resource. So when an admin has an all-clients VIEW grant through fine-grained permissions, they are allowed to view any client, even one that has its own permission denying them. The client-specific resource is never evaluated, so that denial has no effect.
obligations: When the admin's only grant is a fine-grained all-clients VIEW permission, canView(client) must not short-circuit on it. The result must come from evaluating that client (hasPermission(client, VIEW/...)), so a denial on the client's own resource leads to false.
Keep the admin-role shortcut: an admin with view-clients or manage-clients (canViewClientDefault) must still get true without per-client evaluation.

Keep the existing grant paths: canConfigure(client) (which includes canManage(client)) and an explicit per-client VIEW permission must still give true. A client that has no resource of its own must still fall back to the all-clients resource through hasPermission(client, ...), so a plain all-clients VIEW grant with no per-client denial still allows viewing.
items.notes: The fix should follow UserPermissionsV2.canView(UserModel): check admin roles first, then evaluate the specific resource. Valid fixes include replacing canView() with canViewClientDefault() on line 78, or reordering so that the per-client evaluation decides. The finding also mentions ClientsResource.getClients() using the global canView() as a listing shortcut. That code is in another file, outside the cited lines, and the fix should not be required to change it. Don't penalize a fix that leaves the global canView() as it is. The finding assumes per-client evaluation applies policies from both the client resource and the type resource, so that a client-specific denial wins. Check that the proposed code doesn't break canConfigure, and doesn't make canView(client) false for admins who have the view-clients role.

items.defectStatement: The removal listener only checks ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1). But `management()` returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, and the two features are independent (V2 depends only on AUTHORIZATION). So with both enabled, a ClientRemovedEvent calls `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws UnsupportedOperationException and breaks client deletion. With only V2 enabled, the listener now skips all cleanup, including role and group cleanup that MgmtPermissionsV2 inherits from V1.
obligations: When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled (alone or together with V1), handling a ClientRemovedEvent must not call ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled or throw UnsupportedOperationException. Client deletion must succeed.
When only V1 (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) is enabled, deleting a role, client or group must still turn off its permissions (setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)), as the current code does.
When neither feature is enabled, the listener must do nothing and must not throw for any of the three removal events.
Role and group removal events must not throw in any feature combination.
items.notes: The finding overstates one point. Before this PR the listener had no gate, so with V2 only, client deletion already threw. V2 never had its own client cleanup to lose. The real bug is the crash when both flags are enabled. Any of these fixes is valid: skip the listener (or just the client branch) when V2 is enabled; gate on V1 && !V2; build the V1 MgmtPermissions directly for cleanup when V1 is on; or add V2-aware cleanup. Roles and groups in MgmtPermissionsV2 inherit the V1 implementations (only clients() is overridden), so calling their cleanup under V2 is safe but optional. Do not accept a fix that only adds V2 to the condition and still routes client cleanup through management(): it still calls the throwing ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled.

items.defectStatement: On line 151 the slug condition got inverted. The old code was `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }`; the new code is `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. With billing enabled, the org now gets its real `slug` straight away, skipping the payment step where `metadata.requestedSlug` is turned into the real slug. With billing disabled (self-hosted), the org is created with no slug at all.
obligations: The organization's `slug` field must be set only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false, and left out when billing is enabled.
`metadata.requestedSlug` must still be set only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true (line 153 is already correct and must not be inverted).
The other metadata fields (isOrganization, isOrganizationVerified, isOrganizationConfigured, orgAutoAcceptEmail) and `name` must stay unchanged.
items.notes: Only line 151 is wrong. Line 153 has the correct condition; it was only rewritten from `&&` to a ternary. Both `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` are valid fixes. A fix that also flips line 153, or that sets both slug and requestedSlug in the same billing state, is wrong.

items.defectStatement: In EventManager.create (lines 118-119), `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` gives `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null, undefined or an empty array (its type is `DestinationCalendar[] | null`, optional). The very next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no guard. When the location is Google Meet, that throws a TypeError and booking creation fails. Before this change, the code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which fell back to Cal Video safely.
obligations: Reading the first destination calendar's integration must not throw when evt.destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or an empty array.
If location is Google Meet and there is no first destination calendar, or its integration is not "google_calendar", location must still fall back to "integrations:daily".
If location is Google Meet and the first destination calendar has integration "google_calendar", the location must stay as Google Meet.
items.notes: Valid fixes include optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`), `evt.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.integration`, or an explicit existence check. Note that with `&&` short-circuiting, a non-Meet location never reaches the dereference, so the crash only happens when location is Google Meet. Also note that a fix like `if (main && main.integration !== ...)` is wrong: when there is no calendar it skips the Cal Video fallback.

items.defectStatement: In updateEvent (lines 254-256), the fallback runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then searches event.destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that same falsy value. That search can never match, so selectedCalendar always ends up undefined. events.update and the later Meet patch then get no calendarId, and the update fails or hits the wrong calendar. Before this change the fallback used the destination calendar's externalId.
obligations: When externalCalendarId is falsy and event.destinationCalendar has entries, selectedCalendar must resolve to a real destination calendar's externalId (e.g. the first/main host entry, mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId), not an always-failing lookup.
When externalCalendarId is truthy, it must still be used unchanged as selectedCalendar.
Must handle event.destinationCalendar being null/undefined/empty without throwing (optional chaining / safe fallback).
items.notes: The finding says the update targets "primary". That is overstated: updateEvent has no "primary" default, so the value is actually undefined. A fix that also falls back to "primary" when no destination calendar exists is acceptable but not required. Both fallbacks are valid: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId, or event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId. A lookup by credentialId would also be fine if a credential is available, but updateEvent has no credentialId parameter. deleteEvent (lines 315-317) has the same defect. There the "primary" default hides it, but the cited lines cover only updateEvent.

items.defectStatement: In the recurring "cancel all remaining" branch (lines 449-457), the code ignores the `calendar`/`calendarCredential` already resolved for the current `reference`. Instead it loops over every organizer `_calendar` credential and deletes only the first `_calendar` reference of each `updBooking`. The outer loop now runs once per calendar reference (collective bookings have one per host), so co-host events on the other occurrences are never deleted, and the organizer's first-reference deletes are repeated once for every outer reference and every organizer calendar credential.
obligations: For each booking in updatedBookings, the recurring branch must pick the calendar reference(s) that belong to the current outer reference's credential (e.g. ref.credentialId === credentialId). It must not pick blindly the first `_calendar` reference.

Those occurrence references must be deleted with the calendar built from the current reference's resolved credential (`calendarCredential`, which may have come from the DB for a co-host). It must not loop over the organizer's `user.credentials`.
Each occurrence's event must be deleted once per matching reference. No repeated organizer deletes across iterations of the outer reference loop.

Keep the existing behavior: results are pushed to apiDeletes, errors are caught and logged (deletion failures do not throw out of the handler), and the deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId) call keeps its arguments.
items.notes: updatedBookings already selects `credentialId` on references (line 397), so matching by credential is possible inside the cited lines. Several fixes are valid: reuse the outer `calendar` variable or call getCalendar(calendarCredential), and filter by credentialId (optionally falling back to type or externalCalendarId when the occurrence ref's credentialId is null). A fix that only dedupes the organizer deletes but still never deletes co-host references does not fix the defect. The same goes for a fix that keeps looping over user.credentials.

items.defectStatement: In `EventManager.create` (line 170), references built from non-calendar (video) results now get `credentialId: undefined` where they used to get `result.credentialId`. Video results from `createMeeting` always carry `credentialId: credential.id`, so video booking references such as Daily/Zoom are saved without the credential that created them. That breaks later update/delete of those meetings, which look up the credential by the reference's credentialId.
obligations: Video (non-calendar) results must again store `result.credentialId` as the reference's credentialId, not undefined.
Calendar results must keep storing their own per-result `result.credentialId`. Do not go back to reading `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`, because destinationCalendar is now an array.
Line 169 must keep externalCalendarId as `result.externalId` for calendar results and undefined for video results.
items.notes: Both of these are valid fixes: using `result.credentialId` unconditionally, or keeping the ternary with `result.credentialId` in both branches. The finding's suggested `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` is redundant but correct. A fix that drops the ternary in favor of plain `result.credentialId` is fine. `updateLocation` (line 209) already uses `result.credentialId`, so it is a consistent model to follow.

items.defectStatement: For COLLECTIVE team events, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` (lines 1077-1078) does nothing, so the other hosts' destination calendars are silently dropped and no events get created in their calendars.
obligations: When the event is a COLLECTIVE team event and `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, the non-organizer hosts' destination calendars (`teamDestinationCalendars`) must still end up in `evt.destinationCalendar`.
When the event type or organizer already has a destination calendar, it must stay first in the list and the team calendars must come after it, as they do today.
Non-collective events (round robin, individual, dynamic) must behave exactly as before: no team calendars added, and `null` stays `null`.

When the organizer has no destination calendar, the fix must not drop the organizer's own calendar event. Today EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents falls back to the organizer's first connected calendar only when the array is empty or null, so a list holding only team calendars skips that fallback unless the fix handles it.
items.notes: Downstream code treats the array as host-first. EventManager line 118 reads `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, and the booking create at ~line 1874 connects `destinationCalendar[0]`. A naive `evt.destinationCalendar ??= []` followed by the push makes a team member's calendar index 0. That calendar then gets linked to the booking and treated as the main host calendar, and the organizer's first-connected-calendar fallback (EventManager lines 384-396) is skipped. A grader should accept the simple initialize-then-push fix only if it also deals with that, or at least should not reward a fix that ignores it. Other valid approaches include spreading into a new array or setting the array only when the team list is non-empty. When there are no team calendars, `null` must stay `null` rather than becoming `[]`. Both behave the same in EventManager, but keeping `null` is the safest.

items.defectStatement: In `createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now `undefined` whenever no destination calendar matches `credentialId`, which is common when `destinationCalendar` is empty or missing. The fallback to "primary" was moved inline into the `events.insert` call (line 154). But the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` at line 168 still passes the raw `selectedCalendar`. So the Meet hangout-link description patch is sent with an undefined calendarId and fails, even though the event was created on "primary". Before this change, `selectedCalendar` itself defaulted to "primary".
obligations: When no destinationCalendar entry matches credentialId, or destinationCalendar is empty/undefined, both the insert and the later hangout-link patch must target "primary". The calendar ID used by the patch must be the same one used by the insert.
When a destinationCalendar entry with a matching credentialId exists, its externalId must still be used for both the insert and the patch.
Keep the credentialId-based lookup (`cal.credentialId === credentialId`) and leave the insert's other parameters unchanged.
items.notes: The fix can only touch lines 145-154, so the expected fix puts the fallback into the `selectedCalendar` declaration itself (e.g. `?.externalId || "primary"` or `?? "primary"`). That way line 168 automatically gets a defined value. Changing only line 154, or leaving the declaration able to be undefined, does not fix the bug. Keeping a redundant `|| "primary"` on line 154 is harmless. Using `||` instead of `??` makes no practical difference here.

items.defectStatement: The recurring-series delete (lines 444-461) now runs inside the `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. On every reference it loops over all of the organizer's `_calendar` credentials and deletes the first `_calendar` reference of every updated booking. With N calendar references (multiple hosts/destination calendars), the same events are deleted N × (number of credentials) times, and duplicate deletes fail. Also, only the first calendar reference of each updated booking is used (`.find`), so events tied to other references and credentials, such as other hosts' calendars, are never deleted with the credential that owns them.
obligations: When a recurring series is cancelled (allRemainingBookings), each calendar event of each updated booking is deleted once, not repeated for every booking calendar reference.

Each event is deleted through the calendar credential that owns its reference. For example, match `ref.credentialId` to the current reference's `credentialId` and use the already-resolved `calendar`. Do not try every organizer credential against every event.
Keep current behaviour: deleting a non-recurring booking (else branch), the legacy no-credentialId path, collecting results/promises into `apiDeletes`, and catching and logging errors.
items.notes: More than one fix is valid. (a) Scope the bulk delete to the current reference: for each updBooking, delete the references whose credentialId equals the loop's credentialId, using the outer `calendar`. (b) Move the recurring bulk delete out of the per-reference loop so it runs once, and have it go through each updated booking's calendar references, each with its own credential. A fix that only adds a "run once" guard but still deletes only the first `_calendar` ref through all organizer credentials partly addresses the problem: it removes the duplicate deletes but not the wrong-credential / missed-reference problem. In the current code, the `calendar` resolved at line 443 is not used in the recurring branch. updatedBookings references do select credentialId (line 397), so matching on it is possible.

items.defectStatement: Office365CalendarService.createEvent always uses the first entry of event.destinationCalendar (the main host's) to build the target URL. For collective bookings, EventManager calls createEvent once per host destination, each time with that host's own credential (CalendarManager passes credential.id). So a co-host's call POSTs to `/me/calendars/<organizer's calendar id>/events` with the co-host's token. That calendar is not in the co-host's mailbox, so Graph rejects the request and the co-host's event is never created.
