The memo dependencies must cover the org value as well as queryOptions, so the key updates when the org changes.
Keep the key stable (memoized) when nothing has changed, so it does not refetch on every render.
items.notes: This file currently has no `organization` in scope, so a correct fix also needs `useOrganization()` (and its import) outside the cited lines. Accept that, as long as the hook is not called inside useMemo. Any org identifier is acceptable: slug, id, or the full path string. The finding is accurate. Other consumers that build keys from makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions may have the same gap, but that is out of scope here.

items.defectStatement: In `gen_request_data` (lines 153-155), error timestamps come from the nodestore event `timestamp` (a float in Unix seconds, set in `fetch_error_details`). They are compared directly with the top-level rrweb event `timestamp`, which is in Unix milliseconds. A seconds value is always roughly 1000x smaller than a milliseconds value, so every error passes the `<` check at the first replay event and is emitted before all breadcrumbs. The merged chronological log sent to Seer is therefore wrong.
obligations: Before the `<` check, the error timestamp and the replay event timestamp must be in the same unit: either error seconds × 1000, or event milliseconds / 1000. With realistic data, an error must come after replay events that happened before it and before replay events that happened after it.

Keep the merge behavior: errors that happen before an event are emitted before that event's log message, the error index only moves forward, and errors left over at the end are still emitted after all segments.
Events with no `timestamp` must still be handled without crashing (the current code defaults to 0), and the comparison must still use the already-sorted error list.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: scale the error timestamp up (×1000) in the comparison, scale the event timestamp down (/1000), or convert the error timestamp to milliseconds when the ErrorEvent is built in fetch_error_details. Any of these is fine as long as the comparison uses one unit. Trap: the existing unit test test_get_request_data and the endpoint tests use seconds for both rrweb event timestamps and error timestamps (for example 1.5 vs 1.0), so a correct fix may change that test's expected ordering. That reflects a wrong fixture, not a wrong fix. Converting the timestamp shown in the log message text is optional; the fix only has to make the comparison correct.

items.defectStatement: Both `zunionstore` calls in add-buffer.lua (lines 47 and 53) leave out AGGREGATE, so Redis uses the default SUM. buffer.py writes each payload with its end timestamp as the score (`zadd(set_key, {payload: end_timestamp_precise})`). If the same payload is in both the segment set and the set being merged in (for example a redelivered or duplicated span), its score becomes the sum of the two timestamps, about double the real value. That breaks the oldest-first eviction done by the later `zpopmin` cap at 1000: the summed member sorts last and is effectively never evicted.
obligations: Both zunionstore calls (merging span_key and merging parent_key into set_key) must combine scores for duplicate members with a non-additive aggregate (MAX or MIN), so the stored score stays a real end timestamp.

Keep the existing merge behavior: the union is stored in set_key with numkeys 2 and the keys (set_key, span_key) / (set_key, parent_key), the source key is unlinked afterwards, and the guarding conditions are unchanged.
span_count must still be the zunionstore return value (the size of the resulting set), so the zcard fallback and the zpopmin cap at 1000 keep working.
items.notes: AGGREGATE MAX and AGGREGATE MIN are both acceptable, since a duplicated payload normally has the same end timestamp in both sets. A fix that only changes one of the two calls is incomplete. Adding `WEIGHTS 1 1` does nothing to fix this.

items.defectStatement: In add-buffer.lua, the loop that follows redirects was lowered from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`, and the comment explaining the limit was deleted. Nothing in the PR needs this. The new 1000-span eviction (`zpopmin`) is a separate cap on set size. If a redirect chain is longer than about 1000 hops, the loop stops before reaching the real root. The span then gets a redirect to an intermediate span and is merged into the wrong set, so one segment is silently split.
obligations: The redirect loop must again be able to follow chains up to at least the old limit (about 10000 hops), or have some other limit that is not tied to the 1000-span eviction cap. The cap on set size must not be what limits how far the loop follows redirects.

Keep the loop's current behavior: it stops when `hget` returns nil or a self-redirect, it still has some upper bound so it cannot loop forever on a cycle, and `redirect_depth` still records the iteration index (buffer.py reports it as a metric).
Leave the separate 1000-span `zpopmin` eviction cap after the merge unchanged.
items.notes: The simplest valid fix is to restore `10000`; restoring the explanatory comment is optional. Any higher bound or a named traversal limit is also fine. The finding overstates how often this happens: chains only get deep when spans of a very deep tree arrive in reverse order, because each `hset` stores the root resolved at that moment. Still, the change narrows correctness for no reason, so it counts as a regression. A fix that removes the bound entirely is not acceptable, because it risks an infinite loop on a cycle. A fix that also changes the eviction cap goes beyond the cited lines.

items.defectStatement: In add-buffer.lua, the cap at lines 62-64 runs `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)`, which removes the members with the lowest scores. The score is end_timestamp_precise, set by `p.zadd` in buffer.py process_spans, and nothing protects the segment's root span. If a segment grows past 1000 spans and the root span's end timestamp is among the lowest (clock skew, or a segment/remote span that ends before its children), the root span is deleted. flush_segments then emits the segment with no span whose span_id equals the segment id, while the `span-buf:hrs` flag still says the segment has a root span.
obligations: The segment's root span (the member whose span_id equals set_span_id, i.e. the segment id) must never be removed by the >1000 eviction; after eviction it must still be in set_key whenever it was there before.
Keep the size cap: after eviction set_key must still hold at most 1000 members (or the existing limit), and the spans evicted must still be the earliest-ending non-root spans.
Nothing changes when span_count <= 1000, and segments that do not yet contain their root span must still be capped correctly (the fix must not fail or skip eviction when no root member exists).
items.notes: Trap: the script never receives span payloads. ARGV only carries is_root_span, span_id, parent_span_id and set_timeout, and set members are opaque payload bytes, so the script cannot simply look up the root member inside the cited lines. Several fixes are valid: (a) pop the candidates, decode or match the one with span_id == set_span_id and ZADD it back with its score, then pop one more non-root member if that is needed to stay at the cap; (b) pass a marker or the root payload/score from Python; (c) give segment spans a sentinel high score in buffer.py's zadd so zpopmin never selects them. Any of these is acceptable if the root is kept and the cap still holds. The finding somewhat overstates how often this happens: root spans usually end last and so have the highest score, so the bug only shows up with skew or with roots that end early. It is still a real correctness gap. A related point worth noting but not required: has_root_span (hrs) is not cleared on eviction.

items.defectStatement: Lines 17-18 turn `.d-header .contents` into a flex container. Its flex item for the topic info is the outer Ember component `<div>` from `{{header-extra-info}}` (header.hbs:94), which keeps the default `min-width: auto`. The `overflow: hidden` / `order: 2` rules live on the inner `.extra-info-wrapper` (desktop/topic-post.scss:518, common/base/topic.scss:29), which is not a flex item. So a long `white-space: nowrap` topic title (`.topic-link`) makes the outer item at least as wide as the whole title. The ellipsis truncation stops working, and the title pushes `.panel` (margin-left:auto, order 3) out of the header or makes it overflow.
obligations: The header-extra-info flex item, i.e. the element that is a direct child of `.contents` (the component's outer element), must be able to shrink below its content width: `min-width: 0` and/or `overflow: hidden` on that element, or the wrapper class and its constraints moved onto the component element (e.g. via classNames).
A long, non-wrapping topic title must still be cut off with an ellipsis, and the `.panel` navigation must stay inside the header on the right.

Keep the flex layout from the change: items vertically centered, `.panel` pushed right with margin-left:auto/order 3, logo and extra info laid out before the panel. Do not go back to floats or remove `display:flex` in a way that breaks this.
Header pages that don't show the extra-info component (`showExtraInfo` false) must still lay out correctly.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: (a) a rule like `.contents > *` or a selector targeting the component element with `min-width:0` (ideally `flex: 1 1 auto` or a shrinkable basis too); (b) adding `classNames: ['extra-info-wrapper']` to the component and removing the inner div, so the existing `overflow:hidden`/`order(2)` apply to the flex item; (c) giving the component a class and styling it. The fix may need lines outside 17-18 (component JS/template or another selector). A grader should accept edits that target the component element even if the cited lines themselves change little. The same issue makes `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` ineffective, since that element is not a flex item. Option (b) fixes that as well, but that is not strictly required. Just adding `min-width:0` to `.extra-info-wrapper` (the inner div) does NOT fix the bug.

items.defectStatement: In src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py, MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses the abstract StatefulDetectorHandler but its body is just `pass`. That leaves four abstract members unimplemented: the `counter_names` property, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. As a result, `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler(detector)`, which Detector.detector_handler calls, raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Before this change the class was instantiable, so this is a regression.
obligations: MetricAlertDetectorHandler must be a concrete class: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` must not raise TypeError, so every abstract member inherited from its base must be implemented.

The class must still work as `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` and accept the `(detector)` constructor signature. It must still be a DetectorHandler for QuerySubscriptionUpdate, and its `evaluate` must keep the base contract of returning a dict keyed by group key.

If it keeps StatefulDetectorHandler as the base, `counter_names` must stay a property returning a list (an empty list is fine), and the overridden methods must match the base signatures and return types (int for dedupe; dict for group key values; a tuple for occurrence/event data). Placeholder or TODO implementations are acceptable.
items.notes: Both fixes are valid: (a) implement the four abstract members on StatefulDetectorHandler, even as stubs, or (b) go back to subclassing DetectorHandler with a concrete `evaluate` stub. For (b), the base `evaluate` now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, so a stub should return `{}`, not `[]`. Returning `[]` would still fix the TypeError but breaks the type contract. Note that `counter_names` is declared as an abstract property, so a fix must override it; leaving it out still fails. No other code subclasses or instantiates this handler.

items.defectStatement: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` (lines 47-65) only rewrites a y-axis column when its lowercased, stripped text is exactly `count()`. Other spellings of the same no-argument count aggregate don't match: whitespace inside the parentheses like `count( )`, and aliased forms like `count() as total`. Those columns are passed through unchanged, so allowlisted error queries from organization_events_stats return unweighted counts for them.
obligations: Equivalent spellings of the no-argument count aggregate must also be rewritten to `upsampled_count()`: any letter case, whitespace around the expression, and whitespace inside the parentheses (e.g. `count( )`).

Aliased count columns (e.g. `count() as total`) must become upsampled while keeping the user's alias as the result key (e.g. `upsampled_count() as total`). They must not be passed through unchanged, and must not silently be renamed to `count`.
The existing behavior stays: plain `count()`, `COUNT()` and ` count() ` map to exactly `upsampled_count() as count`, so the result key stays `count`.
Non-count columns (e.g. `count_unique(user)`, `p95()`, `other_column`) and their order must pass through unchanged. Aggregates whose names only start with `count` must not be matched by mistake.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: a regex like `^count\(\s*\)(\s+as\s+(\w+))?$` (case-insensitive), or using the discover function-parsing helpers (e.g. parse_function / is_function) and checking for function name `count` with no args. Do not require a specific parser. The finding's mention of "parentheses variations" is vague; inner whitespace and aliases are the concrete cases to check. Handling count(column) with arguments is optional and not required. Equations are passed separately (get_equation_list), so they are out of scope here. The existing tests in tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py must still pass.

items.defectStatement: In testCacheIDPForLogin, the cleanup at line 381 (inside the loop that creates idp-alias-0..19) and at line 425 (after creating idp-alias-20) registers `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove`. That targets a provider aliased "alias", which does not exist, so none of the 21 created IDPs are ever deleted. They stay in the shared test realm and can break later tests, including the IDP counts other tests in this class assert. TestCleanup.addCleanup(AutoCloseable) catches and ignores every exception, so nothing is thrown (no NPE). The leak just goes unnoticed.
obligations: The cleanup at line 381 must remove the provider created in that loop iteration (alias "idp-alias-" + i). The alias must belong to that iteration, not a fixed literal.
The cleanup at line 425 must remove the provider "idp-alias-20".
Keep everything else in the test unchanged: IDP creation, organization linking, and every cache assertion and expected count.

The cleanup must not fail the test for providers that are already gone, such as idp-alias-1, which the test removes partway through. TestCleanup already swallows those errors, so any registration through getCleanup().addCleanup works.
items.notes: The finding's claim that a NullPointerException will be thrown is wrong. TestCleanup.addCleanup wraps close() and ignores every exception, so the real impact is silently leaked IDPs. Any of these fixes is valid: a method reference built with the computed alias, e.g. `get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` (fine, because the resource is built right away and i is not captured), a lambda that captures a final copy of the alias, or getCleanup().addIdentityProviderAlias(alias). Do not accept a lambda that captures the loop variable i directly; it will not compile. Line 303 in testCacheIDPByOrg has the same bug but is outside the cited lines, so a fix there is optional.

items.defectStatement: `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` now also requires `organizationId == null || BROKER_PUBLIC == "true"`. That clause is only needed by the Infinispan login-cache invalidation code. The same predicate is returned by `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` and used in `getFederatedIdentityProviders()` to filter the user's already-linked IDPs. As a result, the base (non-organization) bean now hides any linked IDP that belongs to an organization and is not marked public. Before this change it only checked enabled, linkOnly and hideOnLogin.
obligations: `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` and `getFederatedIdentityProviders()` must go back to filtering linked IDPs only by non-null, enabled, not link-only and not hide-on-login. They must not drop an IDP just because it has an organizationId and BROKER_PUBLIC is not true.

The login-cache invalidation in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation` and `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`) must still treat an organization-linked IDP as login-eligible only when BROKER_PUBLIC is true. Changing BROKER_PUBLIC on an org IDP must still invalidate the login caches.
Keep the enabled, linkOnly and hideOnLogin checks and the null check in whatever predicate each caller ends up using.
items.notes: Several fixes are valid: (a) remove the clause from `getLoginPredicate()` and add a separate predicate, or inline the clause, in the Infinispan invalidation code; (b) keep `getLoginPredicate()` as it is and point `IdentityProviderBean` at the original enabled/linkOnly/hideOnLogin predicate. A fix limited to the cited lines that only deletes the clause, with no replacement used in the Infinispan code, breaks cache invalidation when BROKER_PUBLIC is toggled. That should be judged incomplete. The finding overstates the impact somewhat. `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` already adds a stricter organization/public filter, so the regression only shows up when the base bean is used (organizations disabled) while IDPs still carry an organizationId. It also affects subclasses that call `super.federatedProviderPredicate()`. The clause is redundant for the organization-aware bean, not harmful there.

items.defectStatement: In verifySafeHtml, the common-prefix length (`start`) and common-suffix length (`end`) are computed independently, so they can overlap. When they do, `start + end` is larger than the length of `value` or `sanitized`. For example, value="aaa" and sanitized="aa" give start=2 and end=2. The calls `value.substring(start, value.length()-end)` and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length()-end)` then get an end index smaller than the begin index and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The exception aborts the whole verification instead of recording the "Illegal HTML" message for that key.
obligations: For any pair where value differs from sanitized, the message-building code must not throw. Both substring calls must get indices with 0 <= begin <= end <= length, including when the common prefix and suffix overlap (e.g. value="aaa", sanitized="aa", or a sanitized string that is a prefix or suffix of value).
An "Illegal HTML in key ... for file ..." message must still be added to `messages` for every differing key, keeping the existing message format.
Non-overlapping cases must produce the same differing segments as before.
items.notes: The cleanest fix bounds the suffix loop so it cannot reach into the prefix: add the conditions `end < value.length() - start && end < sanitized.length() - start`. In the "aaa"/"aa" example this shows 'a' vs '', which is the real difference. The finding's own suggestion (clamp with Math.min/Math.max) also avoids the crash, but in that example it shows '' vs '', which hides the difference. A grader may accept it as crash-free, but a fix that keeps the real differing segment is better. Any fix that still lets begin > end on either string is wrong, and so is one that drops the message. The crash is real: sanitized can be a shorter string that shares overlapping characters at both ends.

items.defectStatement: tagDeviceUI writes the device's cache key (localCache.SetDefault, line 87) before it calls anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, TagDevice now passes the error up and the anonymous client's Authenticate (client.go:44-46) rejects the request, but the cache key stays. On the next request from the same device the cache is hit, tagDeviceUI returns nil, and authentication succeeds. A device over the limit is turned away once and then gets in for up to 29 minutes, the cache TTL.
obligations: When CreateOrUpdateDevice fails (at least with ErrDeviceLimitReached), no cache entry for that device's key may remain, so the next request from the same device goes back to the store and is rejected again.
TagDevice must still return the error so that Authenticate's errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) check still rejects the request.
Devices that were written successfully must still be cached, so repeat requests within the TTL skip the DB write.
items.notes: More than one fix is valid: delete the key from localCache in the cited error branch in TagDevice (it can rebuild the key with taggedDevice.CacheKey()), delete it inside tagDeviceUI when the write fails, or only call SetDefault after a successful write. If the fix moves SetDefault, the change lands outside the cited lines (line 87), so a cited-lines-only fix will usually call localCache.Delete(taggedDevice.CacheKey()) in the error branch. Either way counts as correct. Clearing the cache on every error, not just the limit error, is also fine. Concurrent requests racing between the cache check and the write are not a required concern.

items.defectStatement: The password check at line 121 only runs when `credentials.totpCode` is empty. The new backup-code branch (lines 131-157) runs before TOTP verification, and when it runs TOTP is never checked. So a request with any non-empty dummy `totpCode` plus a valid `backupCode` for a 2FA user skips both the password check and the TOTP check. Anyone with the email and one leaked backup code can log in without the account password.
obligations: When a backupCode is used to log in a 2FA user, the request must not succeed without a password check, even if a non-empty totpCode is also sent. Valid fixes include verifying the password inside the backup branch, rejecting requests that send both totpCode and backupCode, or verifying the totpCode as well.
The normal backup-code login must keep working: correct password plus a valid backupCode, with no totpCode, succeeds and the used code is consumed (set to null and re-encrypted).

Existing error behavior must stay the same: InternalServerError when the encryption key is missing, MissingBackupCodes when the user has no backup codes, IncorrectBackupCode when the code doesn't match. The TOTP else-branch must also keep working (SecondFactorRequired when totpCode is missing, IncorrectTwoFactorCode when it is invalid).
items.notes: The finding is accurate. Several fixes are valid as long as backup-code logins can no longer skip the password: call verifyPassword(credentials.password, user.password) inside the backup branch and throw IncorrectEmailPassword on failure, reject requests that carry both totpCode and backupCode, or fall through to TOTP verification when totpCode is present. Simply rejecting the combined case is enough, because without a totpCode the line-121 check already runs. Don't credit a fix that only reorders branches or changes the error codes but still lets dummy totpCode + backupCode log in without a password. There is a related weakness that predates this PR and is outside the cited lines: a non-2FA user who sends any totpCode also skips the password check. A fix doesn't need to address it, but mentioning it is fine.
